task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hello, yes... I'm having trouble with my phone. My mobile data isn't working properly — sometimes it stops working completely, and other times it's just very slow. I'd really like to get it fixed, please.

turns.thought: I can help you with that. First, I need to pull up your account — could you please provide the phone number associated with the line that's having trouble (or your full name and date of birth)?
turns.execution_output: User: It's John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I do want to mention — I'm currently in France, visiting. I'm not very good with all this technology, so I hope you can be patient with me.

turns.thought: Absolutely, John — take your time, I'll guide you through each step. Let me look up your account now.

Found it — your line (555-123-2002) is active and you're on the Premium Plan (15 GB, 8.7 GB used). Since you're in France, outside your home network, the first thing to check is roaming. Your line currently doesn't have international roaming enabled. Let me turn that on for you at no cost.

Good news — I've found your account and taken the first step.

**What I found:**
- Your line (555‑123‑2002) is **Active**, and you're on the **Premium Plan** with 15 GB of data.
- You've used **8.7 GB** so far this cycle, so you're well within your data limit — that's not the problem.
- Since you're in France (outside your home network), your line was **not roaming-enabled**. That's a very common cause of data not working while abroad, so I've **turned on international roaming** for your line at no cost.

Now I need to check a few settings on your phone itself. Could you please tell me what you see at the very top of your phone's screen (the status bar)? For example, do you see any signal bars, "5G" or "LTE", or an airplane symbol?
turns.execution_output: User: Let me look at the top of my screen for you... one moment.

turns.thought:
No need to worry — a VPN isn't harmful or malicious. It's a feature (sometimes installed by work or a security app) that routes your internet traffic through a private server. It can make your connection slower or less stable, and it's worth checking as a possible cause.

Let's fix the clearest issue first. Your phone is currently connected to **2G**, which is a very old, slow network type — that fully explains the "very slow" part. Let's move your phone to a faster network:

**Please do this on your phone:**
1. Open **Settings**
2. Tap **Network & Internet** (on some phones: **Connections** or **Mobile networks**)
3. Tap **Mobile network** (or **SIMs** / your carrier name)
4. Tap **Preferred network mode** (or **Network mode**)
5. Select **5G/4G preferred** (sometimes written as "5G auto" or "LTE/4G preferred")

Once you've done that, please look at the top of your screen again and tell me what it now says next to the signal bars (for example "5G", "LTE" or "4G"), and whether the signal bars have changed.
turns.execution_output: User: All right, I'll try... I'm poking around in the settings now. Let me see if I can find that network mode thing.

turns.thought: That's a big improvement! Let's verify it's actually fast by running one of the diagnostic checks on your line. Please hold on a moment while I check.

Excellent — that's a big improvement! You went from 1 bar on 2G to 4 bars on 5G, and you still have 6.3 GB of data left in this cycle, so your allowance isn't the issue.

To be sure it's genuinely fast now, the best test is to check the speed. Could you please open a web page or run a speed test on your phone and tell me what happens — does the internet feel quick now?

One last thing we may want to address: that VPN is still connected. If your data still feels slow or drops out, the VPN would be the next thing to turn off. Since you're not sure what it is, we can leave it on for now and simply revisit it if you notice any more problems.

Does the internet feel fast to you now, or are you still seeing it stop and start?
turns.execution_output: User: I'll run that speed test thing you mentioned... let me see if I can find it.

turns.thought:
That's understandably worrying, but it's actually a useful clue: your phone says it has a strong 5G signal with data enabled, yet nothing is getting through. That usually means something on the phone is *blocking* the data rather than the network failing.

The most likely culprit now is that **VPN** we saw. When a VPN is connected but not working properly, it acts like a tunnel that's collapsed — all your internet traffic goes into it and never comes out. The signal looks perfect, but no data actually flows. That matches your symptoms exactly (including the earlier "sometimes stops working" pattern).

**Let's turn the VPN off. Please try this:**
1. Open **Settings**
2. Tap **Network & Internet** (or **Connections**)
3. Tap **VPN** (it may be under "More" or "Advanced")
4. You should see your VPN listed with a toggle or a "Disconnect" option — tap it to **turn it off / disconnect**

*Quick shortcut:* swipe down from the top of your screen twice to open the full quick settings, and look for the **VPN** tile or a "VPN connected" notification — tapping it often disconnects it directly.

When that's done, please look at the top of your screen to confirm the little lock symbol is gone, then run the speed test again and tell me what it says.
turns.execution_output: User: All right, I'll try to turn that VPN thing off. I'm swiping down from the top like you said...

turns.thought:
Yes, please! Go ahead and run the speed test again now — that will tell us whether the data is actually flowing.

If it works, you should see a download speed result. Let me know exactly what it says, and we'll go from there.

I understand your frustration — we've made real progress (strong 5G signal now) but the data still isn't flowing, so let's keep going. There's still a very likely explanation, and it has to do with you being in France.

Here's the key thing: being on 5G with full bars shows your phone can *see* the French network, but your phone still needs your permission to actually use a foreign network for data. That's a separate switch called **Data Roaming**. On many phones it's OFF by default, and when it's off you get exactly what you're seeing — great signal, but "No Connection."

I've already enabled roaming on your account from my side, so this is just the last switch on the phone itself.

**Please do this:**
1. Open **Settings**
2. Tap **Network & Internet** (or **Connections**)
3. Tap **Mobile network** (or **SIMs** / your carrier name)
4. Look for **Roaming** or **Data roaming** and make sure it is turned **ON**

While you're in that same menu, could you also tell me whether you see anything called **Data Saver** and whether it's on or off? That's another setting that can throttle or block data, and I'd like to rule it out at the same time.

Let me know what you find, and we'll try the speed test again.
turns.execution_output: User: All right, let me try to find that roaming switch... I'm in the mobile network menu now.

turns.thought:
Yes — please go ahead and run the speed test again now. With roaming turned on at both ends, this is the most likely point where it starts working.

Let me know exactly what it says this time.

If it still comes back "No Connection," don't worry — we're not out of options. The next thing I'd have you check is your **APN settings** (the settings your phone uses to reach the data network), which can get scrambled when travelling between countries. So we'll just move on to that calmly.

You're very welcome — glad we got there!

**What we found and fixed:**
- **Roaming was off on your account.** Since you're in France, your line couldn't use a foreign network for data. I enabled international roaming on your line (555‑123‑2002) at no cost, and you turned on **Data Roaming** on the phone itself.
- **Your phone was stuck on 2G.** That explains the "very slow" part. You switched it to **5G/4G preferred**, and you're now getting full 4 bars on 5G.
- **A VPN was connected.** That was almost certainly why data cut out completely at times. You disconnected it.

Your data now reads **Excellent at 275 Mbps**, and I've confirmed on my side that your line is **Active** with roaming enabled. You have **6.3 GB left** of your 15 GB allowance, and your billing cycle ends **28 February 2025**, so you have plenty of headroom.

**A few things worth knowing:**
- Now that roaming is on, your data will keep working while you're in France. It draws from the same 15 GB monthly allowance — no extra line rental.
- I'd leave the VPN off while you're travelling unless you specifically need it (for example for work). You can always switch it back on when you get home, and if data ever drops out again, that's the first thing to check.
- If data stops working again at any point, a quick **restart of your phone** resolves most temporary glitches.

One note about your account, unrelated to today's problem: a second line on your account (**555‑123‑2003**) is currently **suspended**, with a suspension start date of **1 February 2025**. Let me know if you'd like me to look into that — I'd need to check whether there's an outstanding bill behind it.

Otherwise, we're finished. Safe travels in France, and do reach out if anything else gives you trouble!
turns.execution_output:
User: Oh, that other number — 555-123-2003 — I'm afraid I don't know anything about that. That's not my line, so I can't really say. But no, I don't need you to look into that today.

Thank you again for all your help. My internet is working at excellent speed now, which is exactly what I wanted, and I'm very relieved. You've been so patient with me — I really appreciate it.

Goodbye now!

turns.thought:
You're very welcome — I'm glad we got you up and running at excellent speed. It was genuinely no trouble at all; those settings aren't obvious, and you did a great job following along.

That's completely fine about 555‑123‑2003 — we'll leave it alone. If you ever do want it looked at, just ask for us by your account and we can pull it up then.

Enjoy the rest of your trip in France, and goodbye!
